tools.name: Execute Composite Graph (Deprecated)
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use SALESFORCE_POST_COMPOSITE_GRAPH instead. Tool to execute multiple Salesforce REST API requests in a single call using composite graphs. Use when you need to perform a series of related operations that should either all succeed or all fail together. Composite graphs support up to 500 subrequests per graph (compared to 25 for regular composite requests) and allow referencing outputs from previous subrequests using @{referenceId.fieldName} syntax.

input.title: CompositeGraphRequest

items.title: CompositeGraph

graphId.title: Graph Id
graphId.description: Unique identifier for this graph. All subrequests in a graph are transactional - either all succeed or all are rolled back.

items.title: CompositeSubRequest

body.title: Body

method.title: Method

httpHeaders.title: Http Headers
httpHeaders.description: Custom HTTP headers as key-value pairs for this specific subrequest.

referenceId.title: Reference Id
referenceId.description: Unique identifier for this subrequest. Used to reference its output in subsequent requests using @{referenceId.fieldName} syntax.

items.description: Represents a single subrequest within a composite graph.

compositeRequest.title: Composite Request
compositeRequest.description: Array of subrequests to execute within this graph. Maximum 500 subrequests per graph.

items.description: Represents a single graph containing multiple related subrequests.

graphs.title: Graphs
graphs.description: Array of graph objects to execute. Each graph is transactional. Multiple graphs can be submitted in one request.

type.title: Type

phone.title: Phone

website.title: Website

industry.title: Industry

description.title: Description

shipping_street.title: Shipping Street

billing_postal_code.title: Billing Postal Code

tools.name: Create campaign
tools.description: Creates a new campaign in Salesforce. Only `name` is universally required, but org-level validation rules commonly enforce `type`, `status`, `start_date`, and `end_date` as well — omitting them may cause creation to fail.

name.title: Name
name.human_parameter_description: The name of the campaign you want to create. Pick a clear, recognizable title so your team can find and report on it easily.

type.title: Type
type.human_parameter_description: Choose the kind of campaign (for example, Email, Webinar, or Conference) to categorize it for reporting.

status.title: Status
status.human_parameter_description: Set the campaign’s current status (such as Planned, In Progress, or Completed) so others know where it stands.

end_date.title: End Date
end_date.description: Campaign end date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
end_date.human_parameter_description: The date the campaign ends (YYYY-MM-DD). Use this to define the campaign’s timeframe.

is_active.title: Is Active
is_active.description: Whether the campaign is currently active. Depending on org configuration, setting to `true` may require valid `start_date`/`end_date` ranges; violations raise a non-retriable `CANNOT_INSERT_UPDATE_ACTIVATE_ENTITY` error.
is_active.human_parameter_description: Turn this on if the campaign is currently active. Leave it off for planned or completed campaigns.

parent_id.title: Parent Id
parent_id.description: ID of the parent campaign if this is a child campaign.
parent_id.human_parameter_description: If this is a child campaign, provide the ID of its parent campaign to link them together. You can copy the parent campaign’s ID from Salesforce.

start_date.title: Start Date
start_date.description: Campaign start date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
start_date.human_parameter_description: The date the campaign begins (YYYY-MM-DD). This helps schedule and track the campaign timeline.

actual_cost.title: Actual Cost
actual_cost.description: Actual cost spent on the campaign.
actual_cost.human_parameter_description: How much has actually been spent on the campaign. Useful for comparing against the budget.

description.title: Description
examples: This campaign targets new customers in the Northeast region
Q4 promotional campaign for existing customers
description.human_parameter_description: Add notes about the campaign's goals, audience, offers, or messaging. This gives your team helpful context.

number_sent.title: Number Sent
number_sent.description: Number of individuals targeted by the campaign.
number_sent.human_parameter_description: The number of people you plan to contact (or have contacted) in this campaign. Helps calculate metrics like response rate.

budgeted_cost.title: Budgeted Cost
budgeted_cost.human_parameter_description: How much you plan to spend on this campaign. Helps with budgeting and calculating ROI later.

custom_fields.title: Custom Fields
custom_fields.description: Dictionary of custom field names and their values. Custom field names should end with '__c' (e.g., 'Priority__c', 'Region__c'). Values can be strings, numbers, booleans, or dates depending on the field type.
custom_fields.human_parameter_description: Add any custom fields defined in your Salesforce org. Provide a dictionary where keys are the API names of your custom fields (ending in __c) and values are the data to set.

expected_revenue.title: Expected Revenue
expected_revenue.human_parameter_description: How much revenue you expect this campaign to generate. Used for forecasting and ROI tracking.

expected_response.title: Expected Response
expected_response.description: Expected response rate as a percentage.
expected_response.human_parameter_description: The response rate you expect as a percentage. Sets a target you can measure against after launch.

tools.name: Create contact

email.title: Email

phone.title: Phone
phone.human_parameter_description: Provide the contact’s primary phone number for general calls. Use a format that’s easy to dial.

title.title: Title
title.human_parameter_description: Enter the person’s job title at their organization. This helps others understand their role.

birthdate.title: Birthdate
birthdate.human_parameter_description: Enter the contact's birthdate in YYYY-MM-DD format. This can be used for greetings or segmentation.

last_name.title: Last Name
last_name.description: Contact's last name (required field in Salesforce).
last_name.human_parameter_description: Enter the contact’s last name or family name. Salesforce requires a last name to create a contact.

account_id.title: Account Id
account_id.description: ID of the Account this contact is associated with.
account_id.human_parameter_description: Enter the Salesforce Account ID to link this contact to a company or organization. If you don’t have it handy, you can leave this blank and associate it later.

department.title: Department
department.human_parameter_description: Specify the department or team the person belongs to. This adds context for routing and outreach.

first_name.title: First Name
first_name.human_parameter_description: Enter the contact’s first name as it should appear on the record. Leave blank if unknown.

lead_source.title: Lead Source
lead_source.description: Source from which this contact originated.
lead_source.human_parameter_description: Indicate how you obtained this contact (e.g., Web, Phone Inquiry, Referral). Tracking the source helps measure lead generation.

mailing_city.title: Mailing City
mailing_city.human_parameter_description: Enter the city for the contact’s mailing address.

mobile_phone.title: Mobile Phone
mobile_phone.human_parameter_description: Provide the contact’s mobile or cell number for direct calls or texts. Leave blank if not needed.

custom_fields.title: Custom Fields
custom_fields.description: Dictionary of custom field API names and their values. Custom field names typically end with '__c' (e.g., 'Level__c', 'Languages__c').
custom_fields.human_parameter_description: Provide custom field values as key-value pairs. Use the Salesforce API name for each field (usually ending in '__c'). For picklist fields, use the exact picklist value. For multi-select picklists, separate values with semicolons.

mailing_state.title: Mailing State
mailing_state.human_parameter_description: Enter the state or province for the contact’s mailing address.

mailing_street.title: Mailing Street
mailing_street.human_parameter_description: Enter the street address where the contact receives mail, including suite or unit if applicable.

mailing_country.title: Mailing Country
mailing_country.human_parameter_description: Enter the country for the contact’s mailing address.

mailing_postal_code.title: Mailing Postal Code
mailing_postal_code.human_parameter_description: Enter the ZIP or postal code for the contact’s mailing address.

tools.name: Create custom field
tools.description: Tool to create a custom field on a Salesforce object using the Tooling API. Use when you need to add a new field (Text, Number, Checkbox, Date, Picklist, Lookup, etc.) to any standard or custom object without deploying metadata packages. The Tooling API provides direct field creation for rapid development and automation tasks.

input.title: CreateCustomFieldRequest

label.title: Label
label.description: The display label for the field shown in the Salesforce UI.

scale.title: Scale
scale.description: Number of decimal places for Number, Currency, or Percent fields. Must be less than precision.

length.title: Length
length.description: Maximum character length. Required for Text (max 255) and LongTextArea (max 131072) fields.

unique.title: Unique
unique.description: If true, enforce that all values in this field are unique across all records (case-insensitive by default).

required.title: Required
required.description: If true, this field must be populated when creating or editing records.

precision.title: Precision
precision.description: Total number of digits for Number, Currency, or Percent fields (including decimal places). Maximum is 18.

field_type.title: Field Type
field_type.description: The type of custom field to create. Common types: Text (string up to 255 chars), LongTextArea (larger text), Number (integer or decimal), Checkbox (boolean), Date, DateTime, Picklist (single-select dropdown), MultiselectPicklist (multi-select), Lookup (relationship to another object), Email, Phone, Url, Currency, Percent.

restricted.title: Restricted
restricted.description: For Picklist/MultiselectPicklist fields, if true restricts values to only those defined in the picklist (no custom values allowed).

description.title: Description
examples: Indicates the customer's tier level for priority support.
description.description: Optional description of the field's purpose and usage.

external_id.title: External Id
external_id.description: If true, marks this field as an external ID for integration purposes (allows upsert operations and improves query performance).

reference_to.title: Reference To
reference_to.description: For Lookup fields, the API name of the object this field references (e.g., 'Account', 'Contact', 'CustomObject__c').

default_value.title: Default Value
default_value.description: Default value for the field. Format depends on field type (e.g., 'true'/'false' for Checkbox, date string for Date fields).

visible_lines.title: Visible Lines
visible_lines.description: Number of visible lines for LongTextArea fields in the UI. Typically 3-10.

check_existing.title: Check Existing
check_existing.description: If true, checks if the field already exists before attempting creation. Prevents errors when field is already present.

field_api_name.title: Field Api Name
field_api_name.description: The API name for the new custom field. Must end with '__c' for custom fields (e.g., 'Customer_Tier__c', 'Priority_Level__c').

object_api_name.title: Object Api Name
object_api_name.description: The API name of the Salesforce object to add the field to (e.g., 'Account', 'Contact', 'Opportunity', or a custom object like 'Invoice__c').

items.title: PicklistValue

label.title: Label
label.description: The display label for this picklist value. If not specified, uses fullName as the label.

default.title: Default
default.description: If true, this value is the default selection for the picklist field.

full_name.title: Full Name
full_name.description: The API name/value of the picklist entry (e.g., 'Option1', 'High', 'Active').

items.description: A single picklist value with its label and optional default setting.

picklist_values.title: Picklist Values
picklist_values.description: List of picklist values for Picklist or MultiselectPicklist fields. Each value must have at minimum a fullName.

inline_help_text.title: Inline Help Text
examples: Select the appropriate tier based on annual contract value.
inline_help_text.description: Optional help text shown as a tooltip when users hover over the field in the UI.

relationship_name.title: Relationship Name
relationship_name.description: For Lookup fields, the API name for the relationship (used in queries). If not specified, Salesforce auto-generates one.

visible_lines_picklist.title: Visible Lines Picklist
visible_lines_picklist.description: For MultiselectPicklist fields, number of visible lines to display in the UI.

input.description: Request schema for creating a custom field via Tooling API.

tools.name: Create custom object
tools.description: Tool to create a custom object in Salesforce using the Metadata API. Use when you need to dynamically create new object types (tables) in Salesforce with custom fields and configurations.

label.title: Label
label.description: The display label for the custom object shown in the Salesforce UI (singular form).

full_name.title: Full Name
full_name.description: The API name of the custom object. Must end with '__c' suffix (e.g., 'Invoice__c', 'Student__c'). This is the unique identifier for the object in Salesforce.

name_field.title: Name Field

type.title: Type
type.description: The type of the name field. Use 'Text' for a standard text field or 'AutoNumber' for an auto-incrementing number field.

label.title: Label
label.description: The label displayed for the name field in the Salesforce UI.

display_format.title: Display Format
display_format.description: Format for AutoNumber fields (e.g., 'INV-{0000}'). Only used when type is 'AutoNumber'. The {0000} represents the auto-incrementing number with leading zeros.

starting_number.title: Starting Number
starting_number.description: Starting number for AutoNumber fields. Only used when type is 'AutoNumber'. Defaults to 1 if not specified.

name_field.description: Configuration for the name field of the custom object. Every custom object requires a name field.

description.title: Description
description.description: Optional description of the custom object's purpose and usage.

plural_label.title: Plural Label
plural_label.description: The plural form of the label shown in the Salesforce UI when referring to multiple records.

sharing_model.title: Sharing Model
sharing_model.description: Defines default record-level sharing. 'ReadWrite' allows all users to read and edit, 'Read' allows read-only access, 'Private' restricts to owner only, 'ControlledByParent' inherits from parent object.

enable_reports.title: Enable Reports
enable_reports.description: If true, enables reporting on this object. Allows users to create reports and dashboards with this object's data.

deployment_status.title: Deployment Status
deployment_status.description: Deployment status of the custom object. 'Deployed' makes it available to all users, 'InDevelopment' restricts access to admins and developers only.

enable_activities.title: Enable Activities
enable_activities.description: If true, enables tasks and events for this object. Allows users to track activities related to records.

tools.name: Create lead
tools.description: Creates a new lead in Salesforce. `LastName` and `Company` are required. Org-level validation rules (e.g., email format, custom required fields) may reject requests beyond these; inspect the error response body for the failing field. The created lead `id` is returned in a response wrapper, not at the top level.

City.title: City
City.human_parameter_description: Enter the city for the address. This helps complete the mailing details.

Email.title: Email
Email.human_parameter_description: Enter the lead's email address so you can contact them and avoid duplicates.

Phone.title: Phone
Phone.human_parameter_description: Provide a phone number where the lead can be reached. Include the country code if international.

State.title: State
State.human_parameter_description: Enter the state or province for the address. Use the full name or abbreviation.

Title.title: Title
Title.description: Lead's job title. Maximum length is 128 characters.
Title.human_parameter_description: Add the lead's job role or title, like 'VP Sales.' This helps qualify the lead and tailor outreach.

Rating.title: Rating
Rating.human_parameter_description: Indicate how hot or cold the lead is (e.g., Hot, Warm, Cold) to prioritize follow-up.

Status.title: Status
Status.human_parameter_description: Choose the current status of the lead (e.g., New, Working). This tracks progress in your sales process.

Street.title: Street
Street.human_parameter_description: Provide the street address for the lead or their company. Include suite or unit if applicable.

Company.title: Company
Company.description: Lead's company name. Required - must be provided to create a lead.
Company.human_parameter_description: Provide the company or organization the lead works for. This is required to save the lead in Salesforce.

Country.title: Country
Country.human_parameter_description: Enter the country for the address. Spell it as you would in a mailing address.

Website.title: Website
Website.human_parameter_description: Share the lead's company website URL. This gives helpful context about the business.

Industry.title: Industry
Industry.human_parameter_description: Select the industry the lead's company operates in. Useful for segmentation and reporting.

LastName.title: Last Name
LastName.description: Lead's last name. Required - must be provided to create a lead.
LastName.human_parameter_description: Enter the lead's family name. Salesforce requires this to create a new lead.

FirstName.title: First Name
FirstName.human_parameter_description: Type the lead's given name. This helps personalize communications and match records.

LeadSource.title: Lead Source
LeadSource.human_parameter_description: Specify how you obtained the lead, such as Web or Referral. This helps measure channel performance.

PostalCode.title: Postal Code
PostalCode.human_parameter_description: Enter the ZIP or postal code for the address. This improves mailing accuracy and geolocation.

CustomFields.title: Custom Fields
CustomFields.description: Dictionary of custom field API names and their values. Custom field names typically end with '__c' (e.g., 'Level__c', 'Languages__c'). Use this to set any custom fields defined in your Salesforce org.
CustomFields.human_parameter_description: Provide a dictionary of custom field names (ending in __c) and their values to set custom fields on the lead.

AnnualRevenue.title: Annual Revenue
AnnualRevenue.human_parameter_description: Estimate the company's annual revenue. This helps assess account size and potential value.

allow_duplicates.title: Allow Duplicates
allow_duplicates.description: When True, allows creating duplicate leads even if Salesforce duplicate detection rules are triggered. When False (default), creation fails if duplicates are detected and returns duplicate information in the response.
allow_duplicates.human_parameter_description: Set to true to override duplicate detection rules and force create the lead even if duplicates exist.

NumberOfEmployees.title: Number Of Employees
NumberOfEmployees.description: Number of employees at lead's company.
NumberOfEmployees.human_parameter_description: Enter how many employees the company has. Used for qualification and segmentation.

tools.name: Create note
tools.description: Creates a new note attached to a Salesforce record with the specified title and content. Does not deduplicate — identical calls create duplicate notes. High-volume creation can trigger REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; apply exponential backoff on retries.

body.title: Body
examples: Discussed product features and pricing. Customer is interested in premium plan.
Called customer at 2pm. They requested a follow-up next week.
Important: Contract expires on Dec 31st. Need to start renewal discussions.
body.description: Body/content of the note. Can contain detailed text information.
body.human_parameter_description: Write the main content of the note. Add details, decisions, and follow-ups you want to remember.

title.title: Title
title.description: Title of the note (required field in Salesforce).
title.human_parameter_description: What you want to call the note. Keep it short so it's easy to find later.

owner_id.title: Owner Id
owner_id.description: ID of the user who will own the note. Defaults to the current user if not specified.
owner_id.human_parameter_description: Who should own this note. Enter a Salesforce User ID to assign it to someone else, or leave blank to assign it to yourself.

parent_id.title: Parent Id
parent_id.description: ID of the record to attach the note to (required field in Salesforce). Can be any record that supports notes like Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, etc.
parent_id.human_parameter_description: The record you want to attach this note to. Paste the Salesforce ID of the Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, or other record where the note should live.

is_private.title: Is Private
is_private.description: Whether the note should be private (only visible to owner and users with Modify All Data permission).
is_private.human_parameter_description: Choose whether only you (and admins with full access) can see this note. Turn this on for sensitive information.

custom_fields.title: Custom Fields
custom_fields.description: Dictionary of custom field API names and their values. Custom field names typically end with '__c' (e.g., 'Priority__c', 'Category__c'). Use this to set any custom fields defined on the Note object in your Salesforce org.
custom_fields.human_parameter_description: Add any custom fields your organization has defined for Notes. Enter field API names (ending in __c) and their values as key-value pairs.

tools.name: Create opportunity

name.title: Name

type.title: Type

amount.title: Amount

next_step.title: Next Step

account_id.title: Account Id

close_date.title: Close Date

stage_name.title: Stage Name

tools.name: Create SObject record
tools.description: Tool to create a new Salesforce SObject record. Use when you need to create any type of standard or custom Salesforce object record by specifying the object type and field values.

fields.title: Fields

examples: SELECT Id, Name, Email FROM Contact WHERE CreatedDate > 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z
SELECT Name, (SELECT LastName FROM Contacts) FROM Account
SELECT COUNT() FROM Lead WHERE Status = 'New'
SELECT COUNT(Id), StageName FROM Opportunity GROUP BY StageName
SELECT Id, Name FROM Opportunity ORDER BY Amount DESC LIMIT 10
SELECT Id, Name FROM Contact WHERE LastName = 'O\'Brien'
SELECT Id, Name, Description FROM Account LIMIT 10
query.description: SOQL query to execute. Must start with SELECT. Field names must match object schema exactly — use SALESFORCE_GET_ALL_FIELDS_FOR_OBJECT for unfamiliar objects. ALIASES: No 'AS' keyword (use 'SUM(Amount) TotalSales' NOT 'SUM(Amount) AS TotalSales'). AGGREGATES: Without GROUP BY, ORDER BY/LIMIT not allowed (single-row result). COUNT() SYNTAX: Bare COUNT() only valid alone. With GROUP BY or other fields, must specify field: COUNT(Id) or COUNT(fieldName). Example: 'SELECT COUNT(Id), Status FROM Lead GROUP BY Status' NOT 'SELECT COUNT(), Status FROM Lead GROUP BY Status'. NON-GROUPABLE: Long text, rich text, encrypted text, compound address/location fields. NON-FILTERABLE: Long text area, rich text, encrypted text, multi-select picklists, blob fields CANNOT be in WHERE. FIELDS(ALL)/FIELDS(CUSTOM) require LIMIT ≤200. ID values need single quotes. Apostrophes use backslash: 'O\'Brien'.

tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use SALESFORCE_EXECUTE_SOSL_SEARCH instead. Executes a SOSL search query across multiple Salesforce objects. Use when you need to search for text across multiple object types simultaneously.

q.title: Q
examples: FIND {test} IN ALL FIELDS RETURNING Account(Id, Name)
FIND {Acme} IN NAME FIELDS RETURNING Account(Name, Phone)
FIND {tech*} IN ALL FIELDS RETURNING Account(Name), Lead(Name, Company) LIMIT 10

tools.name: Search accounts
tools.description: Search for Salesforce accounts using criteria like name, industry, type, location, or contact information. Always provide at least one filter parameter; omitting all filters returns a broad, slow listing. Owner/territory filtering is unsupported — use SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY for ownership-based filters. Use SALESFORCE_GET_ACCOUNT to fetch complete field data for a specific record. Unsupported filter fields may be silently ignored — verify results reflect intended criteria.

name.title: Name
name.description: Search by account name. Supports partial matches.
name.human_parameter_description: The account name you want to look up. Enter a full or partial name to find matching accounts.

type.title: Type
type.description: Search by account type. Note: The Type field may not exist in all Salesforce orgs. If the query fails with 'No such column Type', either omit this parameter or use a custom Type__c field if available in your org.
type.human_parameter_description: The kind of relationship this account has with you (e.g., Customer, Prospect, Partner). Note: This field may not be available in all Salesforce orgs.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Maximum number of accounts to return. Results are hard-capped at approximately 2000 rows; use more selective filters if the full dataset exceeds this.
limit.human_parameter_description: How many accounts to return at most. Lower this to get a smaller, faster result set.

phone.title: Phone
phone.description: Search by phone number. Supports partial matches. Requires field-level security access to the Phone field.
phone.human_parameter_description: The account's phone number or part of it. Use this to find accounts by their phone number.

website.title: Website
website.description: Search by website. Supports partial matches.
website.human_parameter_description: The account’s website or part of it (like the domain). Use this to find accounts by their web address.

industry.title: Industry

billing_city.human_parameter_description: The city listed on the account’s billing address. Enter a city name to filter matching accounts.

billing_state.title: Billing State
billing_state.description: Search by billing state/province. Supports partial matches.
billing_state.human_parameter_description: The state or province from the account’s billing address. Use an abbreviation or full name.

billing_country.title: Billing Country
billing_country.description: Search by billing country. Supports partial matches.
billing_country.human_parameter_description: The country from the account's billing address. Enter the country name to filter results.

tools.name: Search contacts
tools.description: Search Salesforce Contact records (not Leads — use SALESFORCE_SEARCH_LEADS for those) using name, email, phone, account, or title. All parameters support partial/fuzzy matching, so results may include unrelated records; post-filter client-side for exact matches. Partial matches and common names can return multiple contacts — always confirm the correct contact by its 18-character Id before passing to write operations like SALESFORCE_LOG_CALL or SALESFORCE_CREATE_TASK. A response with totalSize=0 is a valid 'not found' outcome. Provide at least one search criterion; omitting all returns a broad, slow result set. Returned Ids are 18-character strings and must be used as-is in downstream tools.

name.human_parameter_description: Type the contact's name you want to find. You can use a full name or just part of the first or last name.

email.title: Email
email.description: Search by email address. Supports partial matches.
email.human_parameter_description: Enter the contact's email address or any part of it to find matches.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Maximum number of contacts to return. Maximum allowed is 2000; when totalSize exceeds limit, paginate to retrieve full results.
limit.human_parameter_description: Set the maximum number of contacts to return. Lower values are faster; higher values show more results.

phone.title: Phone
phone.description: Search by phone number. Supports partial matches.
phone.human_parameter_description: Enter a phone number or part of it to search for contacts. This checks both main and mobile numbers.

title.title: Title
title.description: Search by job title. Supports partial matches.
title.human_parameter_description: Enter the contact's job title to filter your search, like Manager or Sales. Partial titles are okay.

fields.human_parameter_description: Choose which contact details to return. Keep the default for common info, or list the fields you need separated by commas.

account_name.description: Search by associated account name. Supports partial matches.
account_name.human_parameter_description: Provide the company or account name the contact is associated with to narrow results. Partial names work too.

phone.title: Phone

tools.name: Search opportunities
tools.description: Search for Salesforce opportunities using multiple criteria like name, account, stage, amount, close date, or status. Apply at least one filter to avoid broad result sets. Partial-match searches may return multiple similar records; verify the correct record by Id before downstream use.

name.title: Name

name.human_parameter_description: Type part of the opportunity’s name to find matching records. Use this if you know the deal’s title or a keyword.

limit.description: Maximum number of opportunities to return. Maximum value is 2000. When totalSize in the response exceeds limit, use nextRecordsUrl to paginate through the full dataset.

fields.description: Comma-separated list of Opportunity fields to retrieve. Supports direct Opportunity fields (e.g., Id, Name, Amount) and parent relationship fields (e.g., Account.Name, Owner.Name). Note: Contact.* fields (Contact.Name, Contact.Email, etc.) are NOT valid because Opportunity does not have a direct parent relationship to Contact; use OpportunityContactRole queries to get contact information. Parent relationship fields like Account.Name may be null on returned records; guard against missing nested values when post-processing.

is_closed.human_parameter_description: Choose whether to see closed deals (true) or open ones (false). Leave blank to include both.

close_date_from.description: Search opportunities with close date from this date (YYYY-MM-DD). When computing relative ranges (e.g., 'this week'), derive dates using the user's local timezone to avoid off-by-one-day errors.
close_date_from.human_parameter_description: Show opportunities closing on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Use this to focus on upcoming or current period deals.

tools.name: Update opportunity
tools.description: Updates an existing opportunity in Salesforce with the specified changes. Only provided fields will be updated. Returns HTTP 204 with empty body on success; call SALESFORCE_GET_OPPORTUNITY afterward to read updated values. Updates may fail with FIELD_CUSTOM_VALIDATION_EXCEPTION or REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING — inspect the error message to identify the offending field.

custom_fields.title: Custom Fields
custom_fields.description: Dictionary of custom field API names and their values to update. Use the exact API name ending with '__c'. IMPORTANT for lookup/reference fields: Fields that reference other records (e.g., Contact__c, User__c, Account__c) require a valid 18-character Salesforce record ID (e.g., '003XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' for Contact, '005XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' for User), NOT descriptive names or text. Passing names like 'John Smith' instead of IDs will fail with MALFORMED_ID error. IMPORTANT for picklist fields: Restricted picklists only accept predefined values from the Salesforce org. Use SALESFORCE_GET_ALL_FIELDS_FOR_OBJECT with object_name='Opportunity' to discover field types and valid values.
custom_fields.human_parameter_description: A dictionary of custom field API names and their values. Custom field names end with '__c'. For lookup/reference fields (fields referencing other records), you must provide a valid 18-character Salesforce record ID, not a name or description. For picklist fields, use exact values defined in Salesforce. Use SALESFORCE_GET_ALL_FIELDS_FOR_OBJECT to discover field types and valid options.

Use IDs from fresh search results; stale or manually constructed IDs may be invalid.
opportunity_id.human_parameter_description: The Salesforce ID of the opportunity you want to update. You can copy this from the opportunity URL or a previous list/search.
